To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a G----T mutation in the promoter sequence of a bacteriophage P22 gene causes pseudo-templated RNA transcription in vitro; (2) this transcription is pseudo-templating by the template strand; (3) the mutation creates an A4 sequence in the template strand that is responsible for the pseudo-templating; (4) the pseudo-templated transcripts are poly(U) molecules that are released by RNAP; (5) the RNAP remains bound to
the G----T mutation causes a novel defect, pseudo-templation, which is characterized by the formation of poly(U) chains, and that the mutation causes the formation of multiple molecules of poly(U).

a G----T mutation in the -1 position of an Escherichia coil promoter causes pseudo-templated RNA synthesis in vitro, that this phenomenon is probably due to slippage of the RNA polymerase during transcription, and that this phenomenon may be relevant to certain kinds of RNA-editing reactions in vivo.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms of transcription and translation in eukaryotes, with particular attention to those aspects of the mechanisms that are unique to eukaryotes.
the mechanisms by which RNAP recognizes promoter elements and initiates transcription.
the mechanisms that control the initiation of transcription and with the regulation of gene expression in bacteria.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
pseudo-templated synthesis of poly(U), by a slippng mechanism, is a consequence of an A4 run of bases in a template DNA.

the sar+1T mutation causes RNAP to pause at position +3 and then to resume transcription by adding U residues to the nascent RNA chain, in a manner that is pseudo-templatable by the T4 stretch of template DNA.
a G----T mutation in the - 1 position of a promoter causes pseudo-templated poly(U) synthesis by RNAP in vitro.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a single G----T mutation, at a position in a promoter which is not the start-point, is sufficient to cause RNAP to synthesize a non-coding RNA product.
RNAP is capable of pseudo-templated synthesis, but this mode of transcription is not normally used by RNAP in vivo.
RNAP has a limited ability to recognize and synthesize a run of T: A base pairs in a promoter, but not a run of G: C base-pairs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
RNAP can be made to stutter in vitro and that the stuttering is pseudo-templatic.
the sar+1T mutation causes a novel defect, pseudo-templating, that is different from the well-characterized promoter clearance defect.
the mechanism of transcription initiation is not as simple as it is often portrayed to be.
